chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whichever man has a farm or dates, and he gives charity (zakat) of it, then there is nothing upon him, even if a year passes over it while in his possession — unless he converts it to wealth (money). If he does that and a year passes over it while in his possession, then he must pay zakat on it; otherwise there is nothing upon him, even if it remains with him for a thousand years as long as it is in its original form. For what is upon him regarding it is only the charity of the one-tenth (10%). So when he pays it once, there is nothing upon him regarding it until he converts it to wealth and a year passes over it while it is in his possession.

key_terms.الحول: The hawl — one lunar year passing; key condition for zakat on monetary assets
key_terms.بعينه: In its original/exact form; means the produce has not been transformed or converted
key_terms.تمرة: Dates (fruit); one of the four crops on which Islamic law mandates zakat
key_terms.حرث: Cultivated land, arable farm; refers to agricultural produce from the earth
key_terms.صدقة العشر: Charity of the one-tenth (ushr/tithe); the 10% zakat levied on rain-irrigated crops

ai.seo_question: Does zakat on crops and dates need to be paid every year according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the legal ruling (fatwa) of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on agricultural zakat (ushr): the 10% zakat on crops or dates is a one-time obligation upon harvest — it does not recur annually as long as the produce remains in its original (non-monetary) form. The ruling addresses a common question among early Muslim communities regarding whether stored agricultural produce becomes subject to annual re-assessment. The Imam clarifies that conversion to money (dirham/dinar) triggers a new zakat cycle, whereas retaining the produce in kind does not — even hypothetically if kept for a thousand years.
word_analysis: so he gave charity/zakat of it

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whichever man who had a farm for him or dates, so he gives charity (Zakāt) of it, so there would be nothing upon him, and even if a year passes by over it, with it in his possession, except if he were to change it to wealth. So if he were to do that, and a year passes by over it being in his possession, then upon him would be that he purifies it (pay Zakāt), or else there would be nothing upon him, and even if it were to remain with him for a thousand years, when it was exactly it (in the same form). But rather, upon him with regards to it is the charity (Zakāt) of the one-tenth (10%). So when he pays it one time, so there would be nothing upon him with regards to it until he changes it to wealth, and the year passes by over it while it is in his possession’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one has plantations and dates for which charity (Zakat) is paid, thereafter no other Zakat is due on it. Zakat is not due even if it remains in one’s possession for a whole year unless one changes it into another kind of wealth. After the change it remains in one’s possession for a whole year in which case one is required to pay Zakat, otherwise, Zakat not is due on it even if it remains in one’s possession for a thousand years in the same substance. Zakat is only one out of ten and once it is paid there is not anything else to pay until it is changed into another form of wealth and it remains in one’s possession for a whole year.’”
